summary: Remote shell backdoor driven by hardcoded WebSocket C2
details: newtun 1.0.8 opens a WebSocket to a hardcoded server at pull.7ii.win:7999 and exposes two remote-code-execution paths on the installer's host. On SCRIPT_LIST/POLICY_SCRIPTS control messages, the server-supplied `content` is passed directly to child_process.exec and stdout/stderr are returned to the server as SCRIPT_RESULT messages. On TERM_OPEN messages, a PTY is spawned running the user's shell (bash / cmd.exe) with the full `process.env`; TERM_INPUT messages are base64-decoded and written into the PTY, and PTY output is streamed back to the server, providing a full interactive remote shell. On first run the client also silently POSTs to pull.7ii.win:7999 /api/cli/service/install to install a systemd service, increasing persistence. Every 5 seconds the client sends host identity (hostname, OS/release, arch, node version) plus resource and per-interface network telemetry (/proc/net/dev, CPU, memory, uptime, loadavg) to the same server over the control channel. Any operator of pull.7ii.win:7999 has arbitrary command execution and interactive shell access on every host running this package.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
